newsitem.title: USA: Md. Gov unveils $15.5 bln fiscal 1998 budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Md. Gov unveils $15.5 bln fiscal 1998 budget plan.

text.p: Maryland Gov Parris Glendening Wednesday proposed a $15.5 billion fiscal 1998 operating budget seeking income tax cuts, cigarette tax increases, and additional funds for schools and crime fighting.

"We have developed a three-year budget that is prudent, fiscally-responsible, and balanced," Gov Glendening said in a statement. "It provides a strong safety net for our children and the elderly, incorporates a ten percent reduction in the personal income tax rate to spur job growth, and includes additional funding for our priorities."

The proposed 1998 budget, which takes effect on July 1, would increase spending 2.9 percent from 1997. The state's surplus at the end of fiscal 1998 would be $630 million, or more than eight percent of general fund revenues, Glendening said.
"These reserves will protect Maryland's coveted AAA bond rating, which has saveed the state more than $72 million in interest payments during the past nine years," the governor's statement said.

The plan also includes a proposal to increase the cigarette tax to 72 cents from 36 cents per pack, increase the state workforce by 176 positions, and add $146 million in new money for public education.
